leads.case_for: I could not refute the core pay signal. 1) Independent re-check of the Meta Ad Library on 2026-10-15 (page id 265462261976256, India, active) shows '~180 results'. Click-to-WhatsApp ads (Send WhatsApp message, api.whatsapp.com) run across Sandalwood, Azalea and Iris. Seven of the 27 cards I loaded started within the last 90 days (2026-07-19, 08-14, 08-20, 08-26, 09-11 twice and 09-16). The oldest started 2025-07-17. Lead-form 'Get Offer' ads started 2026-06-19 and a buyer survey 2026-06-20. 2) The number in the ads (875 875 875 7), the website, the Facebook About tab, an influencer reel caption and the wa.me link are all the same line, +91 87587 58757, so the number is theirs. 3) Not a chain, agency or freelancer, and in Gujarat. Identity is cross-confirmed by the website, Facebook, Instagram, Google Maps (corporate office at the same address) and the RERA aggregator listing the Desai founders as LLP partners. 4) Structural reply gap, from the business's own published terms: the contact form promises a reply within 24 hours, the site-visit form says confirmation within 2 hours, and hours are Mon-Sat 9:30-7:00, while Meta ads send people to one WhatsApp line. 5) The funnel is fragmented: click-to-WhatsApp ads, Meta lead forms, website forms (which post to the site's own backend), influencer reels pointing to the same number, and portal listings. There is no chat widget, bot or third-party CRM script on the site (only Google Analytics). 6) The site-form script shows the 'sent' message whether or not the POST succeeds (no status check), which suggests lead capture is not closely monitored. This is observed in the page source. It is not proof that leads are lost. 7) Business-published email and phone routes exist, and the founders are named.
leads.case_against: 1) The need is assumed, not observed. I found no complaint or review about slow replies: Google Maps has 4.8 stars with positive reviews, Facebook shows 'Not yet rated (1 review)', a web search returned nothing relevant (it mixed in Brigade Group), and the Instagram comments I could read logged-out were spam. We cannot tell whether the WhatsApp line already has a WhatsApp Business auto-reply, an API bot or telecallers behind it, because nothing was sent. 2) Pay is a proxy: ad-library India spend is null, ~180 cards are largely duplicated creatives, and Meta marks long-running ads Active, so live budget is unknown. 3) Probable incumbent on the marketing side: influencer collab reels via collabcentraldesk and creator accounts, plus Meta lead-form ads. There is also an open in-house Digital Marketing role. Someone may already own the ad and lead stack, and the founders may not be the buyer. 4) The decision-maker is not directly reachable. The email is a shared info@ inbox plus a Gmail, and the WhatsApp line is the sales line, read by the sales team. Sandalwood sits in a JV with other partners. 5) Marketing claims run ahead of the record, which suggests puffery and possible sensitivity. Site claims of 50+ delivered and 10+ ongoing projects are not corroborated by Houssed (8 projects: 5 ongoing, 3 completed). The Iris ad says 'Possession by August 2026' while Houssed lists 30 Mar 2028. The Sandalwood ad says 'Possession soon' while the aggregator lists 30 Sep 2027. Do not cite possession dates in outreach. 6) A grade A needs observed need. A reply-speed gap cannot be observed without contacting them, so this stays a B on evidence, though a strong one.

Probable existing agency or influencer vendor for ads, and an unknown lead-handling process (a telecalling team or WhatsApp Business app auto-reply is possible). The founders are named but only reachable through the shared inbox or sales line. The Sandalwood JV may add decision-makers.

Offer a 10-minute demo on one project's brochure, for example Azalea. Do not claim their replies are slow, do not cite possession dates, and do not mention the influencer or agency setup.

Using approvedDate on applications from June to October, 130 projects in the five cities were registered between 2026-08-15 and 2026-10-14, which is a better 'freshly registered' list than application date. The honest result is that Google Maps reviews are a weak source for the 'enquiries arrive but nobody answers' signal in Gujarat real estate. No candidate met the strict bar (a dated complaint about no reply, late callback or unreachable staff within 90 days). The three leads above are stacked-signal leads with low confidence, not proven slow responders.

What I ran (about US$1.0 of the US$3 cap):
- 5 Maps place searches (Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot, Gandhinagar), 2 queries x 20 places each, 200 places, about $0.80. The generic queries 'real estate developer' and 'property dealer real estate agency' return mostly tiny brokers: roughly 40% of listings had fewer than 10 reviews and many had 1 to 5 reviews. Rajkot and Gandhinagar are especially thin. There is no review-count filter in the actor, so I paid for lots of noise. A better route is to start from known project or developer names.
- Reviews of the last 90 days (from 2026-07-17) for 29 higher-volume places returned only 81 reviews in total. Zero of them complained about unanswered enquiries. Most places had 0 to 3 reviews in the window.
- Keyword-filtered review scans ('call' and 'response') over about 80 more places for the last 90 days returned only 4 reviews, all positive. Further scans for 'reply' and 'pick' were blocked (see the last point below).
- Lowest-rated reviews (all dates) for about 55 places. The real 'not picking calls / no callback' complaints all turned out to be older than 90 days, so they are rejected as stale: Priority Real Estate, Vadodara (2025-10-12); Nilesh Real Estate Group, Surat (2025-01-30); Property of Gujarat, Gandhinagar (2025-11-15); TheMuslimProperty.com, Vadodara (2026-02-21); OM Estate Broker, Ahmedabad (2024-07-01); R J Estate, Ahmedabad (2024-01 and 2025-02); Sagar Dave Property Dealer, Vadodara (2024, and it also looks like a pre-visit-fee scam pattern); Samanvay Satgunam refund calls unanswered (2024-06-01); Neptune Realty calls unanswered (2023-08-07); Sunfin Realty (2017 to 2021). Big Block Reality (2026-05-19, rude replies) is outside 90 days and not about response.
- Developers' recent 1-star reviews are about possession delays, construction quality and maintenance, not enquiry handling. Examples: Neptune Realty (2026-08-07, two reviews, delayed possession), Samanvay Satgunam (2026-08-25 and 2026-09-19, delays and unfriendly staff), Sheetal Infrastructure (2026-07-05), Parshwanath Corporation (2026-07-05), Anil Bakeri (2026-07-02), Saumya Constructions (2026-05-05). These firms are not included. Neptune Realty (Vadodara, mktg@neptunerealty.in, no WhatsApp or site-visit booking on its website) is the closest near-miss if you want a fourth low-confidence name.
- Rejected as scam: Balaji Property Broker, Surat. Two recent 1-stars (2026-09-27 and 2026-10-06) say the staff do not take calls after a Rs 300 'registration fee', and one reviewer alleges fraud.
- Rejected as already responsive: Gajanan Properties, Gandhinagar. The owner replies to every review within minutes. Sunfin Realty, Vadodara, also replies within the hour.
- High-star brokers (Pooja Real Estate Surat, GJ05, Divya Estate and others) often show bursts of text-less 5-star reviews, for example 4 reviews within 32 minutes on 2026-07-17. Star rating and review count are weak proxies for enquiry flow here.
- A Google Maps Q&A (unanswered public questions) scrape would have been the best on-brief signal, but it was not run. The Apify account then hit its monthly hard limit, so the Q&A scrape and the extra keyword scans were blocked. The compass/crawler-google-places actor also requires a per-run cap of at least $0.50, above the roughly $0.17 left.
- Two WebSearch queries for public complaints about Gujarat builders not answering or not calling back returned only directories and RERA articles, nothing usable.

Suggestion: for this campaign, Meta Ad Library (builders paying for ads that send enquiries to WhatsApp) and GujRERA new registrations are likely to give much stronger signals than Maps reviews. Maps is best used afterwards, to check reachability and how the owner handles public feedback. Apify spend this run is about US$1.0.
